This thread could use some practical advice of what to study.

Striking - Krav maga (((yeah yeah, whatever))) or Systema are focused on practicality. Some schools of kung fu, as well, and to a certain extent Muay Thai though they can get a bit crazy with the high kicks.

Grappling - Brazilian Jiu Jitsu or maybe traditional wrestling. Judo (and related) taught well is good for standing grappling (throws, sweeps, etc), but most judo schools I've seen don't focus on practicalities.

A good MMA school will be a collection of this kind of stuff, but MMA dojos nowadays are like karate dojos were when I was a kid - it was a trend that came and lots of half-asser teachers showed up to cash in. If you're going to go to any kind of real martial arts school, research first.

In any event, quick striking and grappling needs to be your focus. A street fight is usually over very quickly and has a strong bias for whoever lands the first good hit. You need quick, decisive action focusing on what is practical and effective. You need to learn to punch/kick/elbow etc quickly (and defend against same) and you need to learn to grapple (standing and on the ground) for close combat when strikes are no longer possible.

Avoid big jumping spinning shit like Tae Kwon Do - looks cool, fine as a gymnastics kind of sport, but has very little practical application other than exposing the back of your skull, groin, and other sensitive areas to attack.

Beyond the fundamentals, you need to practice. A lot. It works your technique, but also half of fighting is just familiarity with the situation, feeling in control and having experienced this kind of thing before. Dealing with the adrenaline rush and channeling it productively, rather than being alarmed. Find a friend you can spar with frequently, once a week or so.
